newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA suspect taken to hospital in serious state.
newsitem.headline: ETA suspect taken to hospital in serious state.

text.p: A presumed ETA member, detained on suspicion of killing a prison psychologist, was admitted to hospital in serious condition on Thursday after two days of police interrogation, Spain's Interior Ministry said.

Suspected Basque extremist Fernando Elejalde arrived at a hospital in the northern city of San Sebastian with a number of fractured vertebrae and multiple contusions to the face and body, the hospital said.
The Interior Ministry, determined to get to the bottom of events, said it had started a probe.

"The Interior Ministry has opened an internal investigation, which will run parallel with judicial investigations, to find out in the next 72 hours exactly what happened," the ministry said in a statement.

Police said Elejalde, believed to belong to the Basque separatist group ETA, was arrested on Tuesday after an extended gun battle with police as he fled the scene of the murder of prison psychologist Javier Garcia Elosegui in San Sebastian.
Another attacker, a woman, fled the scene.
Police sources suggested the injuries could have been sustained during his arrest as he had been hit by a car during the chase before police captured him.
In addition, they said he had come to blows with police during his detention and a number of punches had been exchanged.
The magistrate in charge of Elejalde's case has extended his detention by 24 hours, court sources said.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed some 800 people in its 29-year drive for an independent Basque state.
